rows.why: The purpose and business value of building or tuning the model, its intended uses, users and the settings it will be released into are written down before the build starts.
Requirements such as security, privacy and safety are set for the model being built or tuned and shape choices from base model selection to release.
The task the built or tuned model performs and the method used (base model, tuning approach, model type) are defined and documented, for example in a model card, with their assumptions and limits.
Each released version comes with documentation telling recipients its knowledge limits, uses outside its intended scope and how its output should be overseen.
The base models, libraries and other third-party components used to build or tune the model are inventoried with their source, licence and intellectual property risks.
Controls are applied to base models and components before use, such as integrity checks and review for poisoning, backdoors and unsafe code.
Each built or tuned version is evaluated for safety before release, for example that tuning has not stripped safety behaviour, and shown to fail safely when used beyond its knowledge limits.
The built or tuned model is red-teamed and threat-modelled for security weaknesses such as backdoors inherited from a base model before release.
Building and tuning runs, base model and component choices, changes and releases are logged so that who did what to each version can be traced.
The energy use and environmental impact of training and tuning the model are estimated and documented.
Recipients of a released model have a way to report problems and vulnerabilities, and those reports feed into how the model is evaluated.
A go or no-go decision is made on whether a built or tuned version meets its purpose before it is released to others.
When a new risk is found in a built model or its base model, such as a backdoor or poisoning, a response and recovery procedure is followed.
A released model version can be withdrawn or superseded, with set thresholds and responsibilities, when it behaves outside its intended use.
The pre-trained base models and the third-party libraries and frameworks the build relies on are monitored for new vulnerabilities and issues, and replaced when they exceed risk tolerance.
Changes to building or tuning integrate recipient feedback and are assessed against requirements and trade-offs before a new version replaces the previous one.
Incidents and errors in a released model are communicated to its recipients, and a version history records each change to building or tuning and why.
